items.title: Operator Room Vancouver: Cash Flow, Demand Planning, and Scaling Past $30M, Dee Agarwal, Tony Yu, Bryce Alderson, Lucinda Holland
items.description:
In this Operator Room Vancouver, four operators (Dee Agarwal/AMA Holdings and Goli, Tony Yu/Vessi, Bryce Alderson/Nutratology, Lucinda Holland/Sacheu Beauty) discuss the real operating problems that show up once a brand scales past tens of millions in revenue: cash flow crises, demand planning failures, pricing architecture, and hiring philosophy, followed by live teardowns of an Amazon listing, a Shopify store, and a TikTok Shop.

 

TOPICS:

  1. Real cash flow and demand planning failures at scale: a $1.6M GST refund held hostage by a tax audit, tariff-driven manufacturing lead time shocks, and repeated TikTok Shop-driven stockouts, plus the specific fixes (negative cash conversion cycles, revolving credit lines, 15-day lead times) each brand now uses.
  2. Pricing and unit economics philosophy: why one operator refuses to grow unprofitably and uses strict line pricing, while another argues Amazon-only sellers should exploit flexible pricing architecture (testing price/TACOS combinations) since they're not bound by retail price matching.
  3. Live teardowns of a real Amazon listing (trailer hitches), Shopify store (plants), and TikTok Shop (nail files/beauty), plus closing Q&A on AI/GEO visibility tactics and each panelist's hiring and firing philosophy.

items.title: Build Your Own 24/7 AI Employee － Shawn Kolodny － SoFlo Chapter AI Boardroom July 2026
items.description:

TOPICS:

  1. The practical setup: running the agent from a Mac Mini (or a portable setup while traveling), connecting it to Slack channels split by topic to avoid context bleed, and using Notion as its central memory and database.
  2. Permissions and guardrails: starting with read-only access and expanding gradually, since giving an inexperienced agent broad write access (in his case, to his Shopify site's code) caused real damage to SEO and site stability.
  3. Why writing a "soul" file with beliefs rather than a rigid rules checklist made the agent feel more like a working partner than a compliance bot, plus the daily cron jobs (sales reports, rush order alerts, ticket triage) now running the business in the background.

items.title: How to Give Claude Perfect Memory － Ramon Gonzalez － SoFlo Chapter AI Boardroom July 2026
items.description:
In this session, Ramon Gonzalez explains why Claude Code sessions seem to "forget" or contradict earlier instructions, and walks through the memory architecture he built to fix it: split memory files, nightly and weekly summarization agents, and a searchable company wiki.


TOPICS:

  1. Why a single CLAUDE.md file quietly fails: it only loads the first 200 lines into a session even if you've written 400 or 500, so important information written past that line simply never gets read.
  2. His fix: splitting memory by subject (PPC, listings, B2B, etc.) so each session only loads what's relevant, plus a two-step nightly and weekly agent process that condenses daily conversation logs into a clean, non-contradictory main memory file.
  3. A company wiki (built using Google's Open Knowledge Format) that sits between memory and live data search, effectively functioning as machine-readable SOPs that any employee's own Claude instance can reference consistently.

items.title: Scaling Past $30M via Amazon, DTC, TikTok & Retail － Miami Operator Room 2026
items.description:
Go behind closed doors at a private, invite-only gathering of elite e-commerce founders and operators in Miami’s historic Morningside neighborhood. This wasn't a conference or a sales pitch; it was a candid, peer-to-peer exchange between leaders managing brands at the $15M to $300M+ annual revenue scale.

In this session, four industry titans discuss the raw realities of scaling, from defending the #1 Best Seller badge on Amazon to navigating the "hot potato" risks of a potential exit. 

Key Discussion Points:
• Defending the #1 Spot: Chris Kjeldsen (CGK Linens) reveals how he monitors BSR every three hours and his willingness to sacrifice $350k in monthly profit to secure a category-leading position. 

• The DTC & TikTok Pivot: David Stark (Coldest) shares the journey of taking a brand from $4M in debt to a debt-free, 130% year-over-year growth trajectory by shifting focus to community and TikTok Shop. 

• Retail Velocity at Scale: Chris Hunter (Koia) discusses the "liquid to lips" strategy that landed his brand in 35,000 stores and his approach to raising $72M in capital. 

• The "Top of Drawer" Marketing Strategy: Hyla Nayeri (437) explains her aggressive organic social strategy—posting 10 times per day—to maintain "brand cool factor" and dominate on Revolve. 

• What Breaks at $50M: The founders dive into the challenges that don't show up on podcasts, including "ghost orders" on TikTok, navigating Amazon’s changing disbursement cycles, and the debate over the 4-day workweek. 

• The AI "Cooked" Theory: A deep dive into the future of e-commerce, discussing whether AI will eventually automate brand building end-to-end and how to use it for efficiency without losing the human moat. 

Featuring:
• Chris Kjeldsen – Founder & CEO, CGK Linens ($325M+ Revenue)  
• David Stark – Founder & CEO, Coldest ($40M–$50M Revenue)  
• Chris Hunter – Co-Founder & CEO, Koia (35,000+ Retail Stores)
